History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
67-year-old man with known heart failure presents with 2-week history of worsening dyspnea, ankle edema, and mild dry cough; assessment suggests decompensated heart failure—diuretic dose increased and investigations arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive shortness of breath.  
• Timeline: Began gradually ~2 weeks ago; markedly worse over past 3 days. Dyspnea now with minimal exertion (walking in house or to shops).  
• Associated symptoms: Mild dry cough; bilateral ankle swelling noted for “last few days.”  
• Denies: Chest pain, palpitations, fever, dizziness, syncope. Appetite and oral intake normal. Urination increased (baseline on diuretics).  
• Review of systems otherwise unremarkable per conversation.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic heart failure (date of diagnosis not stated).  
• Myocardial infarction (“small heart attack”) ≈5 years ago—brief hospitalization; no further details.  
• No other chronic illnesses mentioned.

Medications:
• Furosemide – dose/route/frequency not documented (currently 1 tablet daily; plan to increase to 1 tablet BID).  
• Aspirin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Bisoprolol – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim).  
• Employment: Part-time lorry driver; day shifts only; concerned symptoms may affect ability to work.  
• Smoking: Former smoker, ~1 pack/day for 25 years; quit (date not stated).  
• Alcohol: Denies alcohol use.  
• Exercise: Limited to daily walk to shops; reduced recently due to dyspnea.

Family History:
• Father died of myocardial infarction in early 60s.  
• Mother alive with osteoporosis.  
• No other significant familial cardiopulmonary disease reported.

Physical Examination:
(Exact values not provided in transcript.)  
• General: No acute distress reported by clinician.  
• Cardiovascular & Respiratory: Clinician states chest examination, oxygen saturation, and blood pressure “all OK.” Specific findings/vitals not documented.  
• Extremities: Bilateral ankle edema reported by patient; not described by examiner.

Investigations:
• None performed during consult.  
• Planned:  
  – Blood tests: full blood count, renal function.  
  – Echocardiogram to assess current cardiac function.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Worsening heart failure (suspected decompensation)  
  • Plan:  
    – Increase Furosemide to 1 tablet twice daily for several days, monitor response.  
    – Arrange echocardiogram.  
    – Order blood tests (FBC, renal profile).  
    – Review in 1 week; earlier review if increased breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.  

General Plan Items:  
• Educate patient on warning symptoms and need for earlier contact.  
• Discussed impact on work; aim to optimize symptoms to maintain employment.  

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Exact vitals, detailed physical exam, medication doses, dates of smoking cessation, ejection fraction or prior imaging, vaccination status.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional audio dropouts (names of meds); no major inaudible sections.
